title: SaaS Outage Dispute
question_for_arbitration:
The Claimant, an enterprise logistics provider, enters this dispute to recover direct operational losses, data recovery fees, and an immediate service credit resulting from a continuous 36-hour data ingestion outage on Respondent’s cloud infrastructure. The outage completely halted Claimant's automated shipping pipelines, requiring manual intervention and database rebuilding.

Claimant asserts that Respondent’s Terms of Service fail to offer any valid liability shield, lack a chosen jurisdictional forum, and provide no alternative dispute resolution mechanism, thereby exposing Respondent to full common-law liability in this forum. The parties have consented to DecisionLayer's jurisdiction.

Claimant demands $50,000 in compensation
arbitration_clause: This arbitration shall be administered by DecisionLayer.AI under its Foundational + Strict Contractual Ruleset, subject to the law of New York and the Federal Arbitration Act. The arbitration will be held online through DecisionLayer.ai. Both parties agree to resolve any claims relating to or arising out of these Terms or the Services through final and binding individual arbitration by a single arbitrator. Class arbitrations, class actions, private attorney general actions, and consolidation with other arbitrations are not allowed. The arbitrator may award relief only individually and only to the extent necessary to redress individual claims. The DecisionLayer rules will govern payment of all arbitration fees. Dropbox will not seek its attorneys' fees and costs in arbitration unless the arbitrator determines that the claim is frivolous or brought for an improper purpose.
